subject: Conditional pin and automatic failover for Acme Payments - SLA mitigation
messages:
From: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@acmepay.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Sally Chen <sally.chen@acmepay.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: pin + automatic fallback during staged rollout

Hi Hannah —

We've been testing the new routing variant you proposed and saw two short latency spikes in the last week during mid-day traffic. Acme's SRE team needs clarity on how Redwood will protect our 99.9% P95/P99 commitments during staged rollouts. Specifically, we want to: 

- Be able to pin the stable version for the majority of traffic while a canary (ramped to ~10%) runs newer optimizations.
- Have an automatic failover (rollback) to the pinned stable version if P95 latency increases >30% or error rate exceeds 0.5% for more than 5 minutes.

Can you confirm whether this is supported today as a formal SLA mitigation and what exceptions we need? We also need documentation we can share with our procurement and legal teams.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Mills
Sr. Engineer, Platform
Acme Payments

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Request: pin + automatic fallback during staged rollout

Hi Jordan — thanks for raising this and for the example traces. Short answer: yes, we can support a conditional-pin + automatic-failover policy, but it requires a scoped SLA carve-out and explicit rollout guardrails. 

Proposal (summary):
1) Conditional pin: Configure a pinned stable model (vX) that serves 90% by default. Canary variant (vX+1) runs at 10% for the initial ramp. Pinning prevents background autoswitching when we observe transient errors.
2) Automated failover (circuit-breaker): If any of the following hold for a rolling 5-minute window we will automatically divert canary traffic back to the pinned variant and pause further ramps:
   - P95 latency increases by >= 30% vs baseline
   - Error rate (5xx or rate-limited responses) exceeds 0.5%
   - Token-drop anomalies or KV cache miss surge > 2x baseline
3) Safety timers and human-in-loop: Automated rollback occurs immediately, but we will notify both Acme SRE and our on-call infra lead. A restart of the ramp requires a documented post-mortem attached to the rerun.
4) Metrics and alerts: We'll create the SLO monitors (P95, P99, error rate, tail latency percentiles) and give Acme a read-only dashboard.

Operational items I need from you:
- Confirm the exact thresholds you want (I used your numbers as a starting point).
- Accept a temporary SLA exception for the canary ramp period so the exception is tracked in procurement (we'll capture start/end dates).

I'll draft the exception form + a short playbook (runbook + rollback checklist) and attach it. Looping in Karthik to confirm we can automate the circuit-breaker in the serving runtime.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: pin + automatic fallback during staged rollout

Folks — I reviewed Hannah's proposal and the initial metrics. I'm supportive with two additions: 

1) Add a short cooldown window after an automated rollback: block ramps for 30 minutes and automatically escalate to on-call if two rollbacks occur within 24 hours.
2) Add a graded fallback: first rollback moves canary back to 5% (de-risk), second rollback to 0% (full revert). Immediate full revert should only happen for severe error-class triggers (e.g., data corruption, 5xx surge > 2%).

I can authorize a 90-day temporary SLA carve-out for Acme that allows this conditional-pin behavior provided we document: thresholds, notification channels, and that Acme accepts the carve-out in writing (we'll use the attached mutual action plan).

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Reliability, Redwood Inference
